properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 28 at 6:40PM MDT until July 28 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM MDT THIS EVENING
FOR EAST CENTRAL CUSTER AND WEST CENTRAL PUEBLO COUNTIES...

At 640 PM MDT, Thunderstorms producing heavy rain have ended over
most of the Aspen Acres Burn Scar, though run-off, flooding and
debris flows will continue for at least the next 1 to 2 hours.
Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. Any additional rainfall
amounts this evening will be light, generally less than a tenth of an
inch. Flash flooding is already occurring, with water rescues and
large debris flows reported.

FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for Aspen Acres Burn Scar, including San
Isabel and North Creek near Beulah. This is a PARTICULARLY
DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER
GROUND NOW! Life threatening flash flooding of low water
crossings, small creeks and streams, highways, streets and
underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beulah and San Isabel.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake, Northcreek Road county line to Red Mountain Camp
and Northcreek Road from Red Mountain Camp to Beulah.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 28 at 6:21PM MDT until July 28 at 9:15PM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Kit Carson County in east central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 915 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 620 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
Very heavy rainfall is going on with this thunderstorm.
Hydroplaning will be a concern especially across Interstate 70.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Flagler, Seibert and Vona.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 28 at 5:08PM MDT until July 28 at 8:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 815 PM MDT.

* At 508 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Pueblo, Pueblo Airport, Boone, Blende, Salt Creek, Pueblo
Reservoir, Avondale, Pueblo West, Pinon, Pueblo Depot and Colorado
City.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 28 at 12:13PM MDT until July 28 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive
rainfall over the Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar are possible.

* WHERE...Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar in Ouray County Colorado,
including Dexter Creek and Cutler Creek, particularly along
highway 550, and Cow Creek.

* WHEN...Until 800 PM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall is possible over the Gold Mountain
Burn Scar which could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek. Cow creek may also be affected. The debris flow can consist
of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1202 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Gold Mountain Burn Scar, including Cow Creek, and along
highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter Creek.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
